core_obligations: Construct the duality data (proof lines 4856-4890): for a nonempty equidimensional smooth projective scheme of dimension d, use the Kunneth decomposition of the cohomology of the product, define the unit as multiplication by the class of the diagonal, and define the counit as pullback along the diagonal followed by the degree map of axiom (A6).

Verify the triangle identities (proof lines 4890-4912): the composition of the unit with the counit applied to a class is computed using the projection formula for the threefold product and the compatibility of the diagonal with the projections, reducing to the pairing of the class of the diagonal with the pullback of the class by the first projection, which is the identity by the choice of the degree map; the other triangle identity is proved in exactly the same manner.

Identify the two pullbacks (proof lines 4912-4926): the pullbacks of a class by the two projections agree on the diagonal, and the conormal sheaf of the diagonal is the sheaf of differentials of the diagonal, which is the restriction of the pullback of the differentials of the scheme; the lemma relating the action of the diagonal to the conormal sheaf then shows that capping the class of the diagonal with the two pullbacks gives the same result, completing the proof.
proof_roadmap: Use Kunneth and the class of the diagonal to build the unit and the counit of the duality.
Verify the triangle identities by a projection formula computation.
Compare the two pullbacks through the conormal sheaf of the diagonal.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that axioms (A1) to (A7) imply the existence of a degree map making the graded cohomology of a nonempty equidimensional smooth projective scheme a dual of itself, which is axiom (A) (statement lines 4852-4855). The proof (proof lines 4856-4926) constructs the unit and counit from the class of the diagonal, checks the two triangle identities, and compares the two pullbacks using the conormal sheaf of the diagonal. H3: a duality verification with an explicit computation, written out in full.
